part1.intro: The examiner asks the candidate about him/herself, his/her home, work or studies and other familiar topics.

topics.title: Flowers
questions: Do you like to have flowers in your home? [Why/Why not?]
Where would you go to buy flowers? [Why?]
On what occasions would you give someone flowers?
Are flowers important in your culture? [Why/Why not?]

part2.topic: Describe a meeting you remember going to at work, college or school.
points: when and where the meeting was held
what the people at the meeting talked about
part2.closing: and explain why you remember going to this meeting.

topics.title: Going to meetings
questions: What are the different types of meeting that people often go to?
Some people say that no-one likes to go to meetings – what do you think?
Why can it sometimes be important to go to meetings?

topics.title: International meetings
questions: Why do you think world leaders often have meetings together?
What possible difficulties might be involved in organising meetings between world leaders?
Do you think that meetings between international leaders will become more frequent in the future? Or will there be less need for world leaders to meet?

issues: Speaking Part 2: in the book the last cue-card point and the closing line share a printed line ('what the people at the meeting talked' / 'about and explain why you remember going' / 'to this meeting.'); split as point 'what the people at the meeting talked about' and closing 'and explain why you remember going to this meeting.'. No wording changed.
